standard.title: Angles and Parallel Lines
standard.description: identify corresponding, alternate and co-interior relationships between angles formed when parallel lines are crossed by a transversal; use them to solve problems and explain reasons
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify angle relationships on lines and at points and determine unknown angles (from AC9M6M04). Students understand that angles on a straight line sum to 180° and angles at a point sum to 360°.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify corresponding, alternate and co-interior angle relationships and use them with geometric reasoning to find unknown angles.

nodes.label: Parallel lines and transversals
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students identify parallel lines and transversals in diagrams and name the eight angles formed.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and label all eight angles formed by a transversal crossing two parallel lines.
nodes.typical_width: Draw parallel lines with a transversal; identify corresponding, alternate, and co-interior pairs by position.
wider: Investigate designs and structures where parallel lines and transversals appear (roof trusses, railway tracks, tiled floors).
Use dynamic geometry software to verify that corresponding angles remain equal as the transversal angle changes.

response_modes.reason: Correct identification of angle pairs is prerequisite to all reasoning in this descriptor. Students who confuse corresponding with alternate make systematic errors in every subsequent problem.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who confuse angle pair types (corresponding, alternate, co-interior) apply the wrong property in Nodes 2 and 3 — they may apply the equal-angles rule to co-interior pairs (which are supplementary), producing wrong answers throughout.
success_criteria: Correctly identifies and labels the eight angles formed.
Correctly identifies at least one example of each: corresponding, alternate, co-interior pair.
Does not confuse vertically opposite angles with the parallel line angle relationships.

nodes.label: Properties of corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students state and apply the angle properties: corresponding angles are equal, alternate angles are equal, co-interior angles are supplementary.
nodes.minimum_width: State each property and calculate a missing angle using one of the three relationships.
nodes.typical_width: Apply multiple properties in sequence to find all unknown angles in a parallel lines diagram; give reasons for each step.
wider: Investigate why these properties hold — informally, by translating or rotating the transversal to show correspondence.
Apply properties to real-world geometric problems: angles in roof pitch design, alignment of structures.

response_modes.reason: Students frequently misapply the properties, especially confusing co-interior (supplementary) with alternate (equal). Multiple diagram orientations — not just the standard vertical layout — resolve this.

nodes.hinge_reason: The co-interior/alternate confusion produces persistent errors in Node 3 multi-step reasoning — students who apply the wrong property at step 1 propagate wrong values through the entire chain, with no self-correction possible without restating geometric reasons.
success_criteria: Calculates missing angles using the correct property.
Does not apply the equal-angle property to co-interior pairs.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Understanding why the angle properties hold (via translation/rotation argument) is richer than applying them — advancing students who can construct an informal justification develop genuine geometric reasoning.

nodes.label: Using angle reasoning to solve problems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students solve multi-step angle problems involving parallel lines, giving geometric reasons for each step.
nodes.minimum_width: Solve a problem requiring two steps of angle reasoning and state the reason for each step.
nodes.typical_width: Solve problems combining parallel line angle properties with straight line and vertically opposite angle facts; write full geometric reasons.
wider: Design a problem requiring at least three angle reasoning steps — write the solution with full justification.
Investigate how angle properties are applied in geometric proofs (informal): show that a given pair of lines must be parallel.

response_modes.reason: Multi-step geometric reasoning requires an explicit scaffold: identify what you know, select the applicable property, state the reason. Students who calculate without reasons cannot self-check and lose marks systematically.

success_criteria: Solves a multi-step angle problem correctly.
States a geometric reason for each step.
Does not assume angle values without justification.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Multi-step geometric proof design is a rich task for advancing students — creating problems that require chaining three or more angle facts develops systematic reasoning within the Year 7 band.
